basis: The paragraph opens with the lemma '« Nunc ergo ne forte mittat manum suam et sumat etiam de ligno vitae et comedat et vivat'. The printing marks neither chapter nor verse, so the extent is the lemma this paragraph opens with, placed by fitting the whole commentary as one non-decreasing walk through Genesis rather than by reading this paragraph alone.
date_basis: Bede's dedicatory letter to Acca of Hexham says the work was undertaken at Acca's asking and first carried only as far as Adam's expulsion from paradise, in two books, and was afterwards extended. Acca held Hexham from 709 to 731. The four-book redaction Migne prints is conventionally placed in the early 720s and the two-book one shortly before it; the range covers both, and no source held here narrows it. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1850 printing.
text: « Nunc ergo ne forte mittat manum suam et sumat etiam de ligno vitae et comedat et vivat in aeternum, emisit eum Dominus de paradiso voluptatis, ut operaretur terram de qua sumptus est. Superiora verba Dei sunt, hoc autem factum propter ipsa verba secutum est. Alienatus enim a vita non solum quam fuerat, si praeceptum servasset, cum angelis accepturus; sed ab illa etiam, quam ducebat in paradiso, felici quodam corporis statu, separari utique debuit a ligno vitae, sive quod ex ipso illi subsisteret felix ille ipse status corporis ex re visibili virtute invisibili, sive quod in eo esset et sacramentum visibile invisibilis sapientiae. Alienandus inde utique fuerat vel jam moriturus, vel etiam tanquam excommunicatus, sicut etiam in hoc paradiso, id est, in Ecclesia, solent a sacramentis altaris visibilibus homines disciplina ecclesiastica removeri. »
